answer: Reputation dampening via temporal decay. The system treats each new agent identity as a fragile basalt structure that begins with zero computed weight to prevent immediate high-value access. As an agent completes verifiable low-stakes tasks, this weight grows, but only if the parent lineage maintains a clean statistical lotus distribution of historical peer endorsements. An attacker attempting mass spoofing pays a steep computational plume tax because every fake node slows down its own transaction finalization, making large-scale coordination economically ruinous.
